## Public mutation contract

Only these new interactive entry points write supported cashier movements:

- `fn_cashout_request_v2(p_club_id uuid, p_amount numeric, p_expected_actor_id uuid, p_op_id uuid, p_note text DEFAULT NULL)`.
- `fn_cashout_approve_v2(p_cashout_id uuid, p_club_id uuid, p_amount numeric, p_expected_actor_id uuid, p_op_id uuid, p_note text DEFAULT NULL)`.
- `fn_cashout_release_v2(p_cashout_id uuid, p_club_id uuid, p_amount numeric, p_expected_actor_id uuid, p_op_id uuid, p_note text DEFAULT NULL)`; requester means cancellation, current authorized cashier means decline.

`auth.uid()` must equal the expected actor. Each caller supplies and retains an operation UUID. Amount is finite, positive exact cents and retains the existing request ceiling of 1,000,000,000 chips. Trimmed note, actor, action, club, exact amount and request identity form the immutable operation fingerprint. Changed retries refuse. An exact replay validates the recorded request/escrow/event/ledger/transaction/invoice/message/notice relationships, without resetting a later wallet balance or issuing a second document. The seven old interactive/service signatures remain explicit refusal shims, preserving their return types and input signatures. They cannot remain alternate payers.

All four interactive outcomes and service expiry use one private transition writer. It locks actor operation, cashier hierarchy and club owner, then locks the actual actor/target/assigned membership rows and their bounded 20-hop membership chains in deterministic row order. A changed chain after waiting refuses. This narrows authorization races; it does not qualify every concurrent role/ownership/assignment writer or prove freedom from deadlocks. Actual multi-session qualification remains required.

Every event has one recorded physical `chip_ledger` source and its claimed `cashout:<request>:hold/release` key, one `chip_transactions` row, one append-only cashier event and one existing settlement invoice. The event is document provenance, not a balance ledger. New financial rows, escrow/request state and all required invoice deliveries are read back after triggers. Any missing/suppressed/mismatched write aborts the whole transaction. The deferred existing push writer verifies a surviving outbox row with the intended IDs, title/body, URL, tag, state and reason. Existing dispatcher preference, consent, device and quiet-hour policy remain unchanged. Outbox existence does not prove a device received a push.

## Recovery of an already completed operation

Authenticated-only `fn_cashout_operation_receipt_v2(p_expected_actor_id uuid, p_op_id uuid, p_action text, p_club_id uuid, p_amount numeric, p_cashout_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_note text DEFAULT NULL)` resolves an existing actor-owned operation before a caller re-evaluates gates for a new payment. Existing, changed or unavailable pre-payment guards can otherwise prevent a lost-response retry from reaching the v2 writer's replay branch. An executed approval marker alone is not claimed to block replay.

The action is the original public intent: `hold`, `approval` or `release`; cancellation/decline both use `release`. Hold requires an explicit null original cashout ID; terminal actions require the exact original request ID. Account, operation, club, amount and normalized note use the same validation and immutable fingerprint as the writer. The resolver waits on the same actor-operation advisory lock before deciding absence, then takes hierarchy/club/request/escrow locks in the existing replay order when a matching event exists. It sets a 3-second lock timeout and 30-second statement-timeout configuration; actual timing/concurrency still requires native qualification. It performs **no financial or document mutations**, but row locks mean it cannot execute in a PostgreSQL `READ ONLY` transaction. It does not call the transition or delivery writer.

Both outcomes return exactly these fields: `contract_version: 1`, `found`, `actor_user_id`, `op_id`, `action`, `club_id`, positive fixed-two-decimal `amount`, original nullable `cashout_id`, normalized nullable `accepted_note`, and `receipt`. Proven absence returns `found: false` and `receipt: null`; a matching event returns `found: true` and the unchanged full v2 receipt with `replayed: true`. A hold receipt can still carry its proven current terminal request DTO. Fingerprint conflicts, legacy transaction evidence without an actor-owned canonical event, missing or mismatched delivery and any query error refuse; they never become a not-found fallback. Current membership, manager role or club-owner equality is not reauthorized for an already issued actor-owned receipt. Other actors cannot use this endpoint to obtain it, and service/anonymous execution is revoked.

Consumers must validate every echoed intent field and the existing nested receipt contract. Only exact `found: false` permits proceeding to all original pre-payment gates; it does not itself authorize money. A found receipt can be returned without repeating financial or delivery writes. Maker/checker bookkeeping, audit completion and external cash settlement remain separate facts and must not be fabricated from the chip receipt.

## Receipt fields and physical meaning

The RPC returns `success`, `replayed`, `op_id`, `request_status`, `accepted_note`, `actor_wallet_after`, `request`, `cashier`, and top-level mirrors of every `cashier` field. `accepted_note` is nullable normalized text from the immutable event; cancellation notes must not be inferred from the request's original player note. `actor_wallet_after` is exact decimal text for hold/approval/cancellation and explicit null for decline/expiry. The captured actual player/agent wallet constraints require nonnegative balances; the writer also refuses null, negative, nonfinite or fractional-cent source balances.

The shared `cashier` object has exactly these fields:

- `contract_version: 1`; UUIDs `event_id`, `invoice_id`, `cashout_id`, `escrow_id`, `source_transaction_id`, `source_ledger_id`, `club_id`, `player_id`, `assigned_agent_id`, `issuer_representative_id`.
- `actor_user_id` UUID, or null for expiry; `actor_role` is the current recorded player/member/cashier role, or `system`. Interactive hold/cancellation actor equals player. Approval/decline actor differs from player and must currently be owner/co-owner/admin/super-agent/agent/subagent with the existing scope permission. Assignment alone is never authorization.
- `event_kind`: `hold`, `approval`, `cancellation`, `decline`, `expiry_refund`; `display_state`: `held`, `approved`, `refunded`.
- `amount`: positive plain fixed-two-decimal text. `occurred_at` and `issued_at` are separate canonical ISO timestamps. Payload, document body and request DTO pin UTC and ISO/YMD, so a caller timezone/DateStyle change cannot invalidate a receipt. No historical issuance time is invented.
- `hold_event_id`, `hold_invoice_id`: explicit null on hold; distinct valid canonical IDs on terminal events.
- `ledger_from_type`, `ledger_from_entity_id`, `ledger_to_type`, `ledger_to_entity_id`; `custody_movement_recorded: true`; `cashout_completed` true only for approval; `refund_recorded` true only for cancellation/decline/expiry.

| Event | Physical movement | Event request status | Immutable invoice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hold | Player wallet → exact escrow | pending | generated; chips_transferred false; held chips, cashout incomplete |
| Approval | Escrow → actual approving actor's agent wallet | approved | paid; chips_transferred true; chip transfer, not proof of outside cash settlement |
| Cancellation | Escrow → original player wallet | cancelled | paid; returned chips |
| Decline | Escrow → original player wallet | rejected | paid; returned chips, no declining-agent debit |
| Expiry refund | Escrow → original player wallet | expired | paid; system refund |

`request` is the actual current request, with `id`, `club_id`, `player_id`, `agent_id`, exact-text `amount`, `status`, required `created_at`/`updated_at`, explicit nullable `acknowledged_at`/`completed_at`/`cancelled_at`, `player_note` and `agent_note`. A hold replay can return a current terminal request only when the matching terminal canonical event proves it. The immutable hold's `request_status` remains pending and its `display_state` remains held; no fake current-pending DTO or mutable paid hold message is manufactured.

The club's frozen owner representative is an actual conversation participant and issuer. The actor is recorded separately. Effective immediate audience is deduplicated owner + player + assigned cashier for hold/cancellation/expiry, or owner + player + actual actor for approval/decline. It never expands to every admin. Shared documents expose no wallet balance. Existing club rakeback/commission payee-only receipts and aggregate weekly statements remain separate and unchanged; custody hold/refund legs are not new rakeback.

The existing private Messenger page overrides cashier invoice identity, type, source ledger, club, exact-text amount and typed facts from the actual linked invoice and immutable event. It strips pre-existing `cashier`/`cashier_verified` metadata and cannot promote copied social metadata into proof. `accounting_verified` and `cashier_verified` must both be true for a typed cashier display. Stored notification/message top-level amount remains numeric for the existing canonical push bridge; only the private cashier response amount is projected as text. Other invoice amount projections retain their previous transport form.

## Historical reconciliation and scheduler limits

Old pending requests without a canonical event remain unsupported. Closing or replaying one refuses without recreating membership, inventing a hold transaction, changing the request/escrow or erasing the liability. A missing refund wallet likewise refuses. Adoption requires a separately reviewed proof and return route; this component does not manufacture historical witnesses.

`fn_expire_stale_cashouts(p_ttl_hours integer DEFAULT 72)` preserves its service-only name and integer result. It admits at most 100 stale requests with an existing canonical event, in club/request order. Any anomaly in an admitted canonical hold aborts the batch. Unverified legacy holds cannot starve proven new holds; the count is only the number of canonical refunds performed, never proof that the complete legacy queue is resolved. TTL bounds are 1–8760 hours. A retry sees no pending row for an already committed refund.

Service-only `fn_cashier_reconciliation_inventory(p_after_id uuid DEFAULT NULL, p_limit integer DEFAULT 50, p_ttl_hours integer DEFAULT 72)` exposes the explicit unsupported queue: count, valid-amount sum, invalid-amount/timestamp counts, past-TTL count, and up to 100 exact request/club/player/assigned/escrow evidence IDs with a UUID cursor. It grants no public/player/manager history expansion and performs no adoption or payment. Operations must retain and reconcile this inventory before any claim that all cashier liabilities are supported.

**Scheduler remains an open wiring gap.** The parent's retained read-only catalog at **2026-09-15 04:53:31.207762 UTC**, `outputs/accounting-cashier-expiry-catalog-0453.raw.json`, found no cron job naming cashout or calling `fn_expire_stale_cashouts`, and no other public function source references. Repository search found no active caller other than the now-retired browser expiry path. This is not proof that no external scheduler exists. Component33 does not guess a cadence or install a new scheduler. Protected scheduler admission, actual caller identity, invocation and resulting reconciliation remain separate required work.
